summit.title: Two stars and a Bib, three towns
summit.story: The Jura's starred cooking sits on the roads north of Lons, not in the town. In Pupillin, the Ploussard village, Vivien Sonzogni and his partners took over the Grapiot in 2024 and won its first MICHELIN star in March 2026; Gault&Millau singles out the Bresse hen with morels. In Arbois, by the Cuisance, Jérôme Brousseau cooks and Lisa Vuillemin makes the desserts at Le Bistronôme, a Bib Gourmand known for Planches trout with morels in Vin Jaune. In Dole, about 50 km north, Laurent Barberot took over La Chaumière in 2025 and serves its starred menu only from Friday to Saturday evening. Port-Lesney's old two-star table is gone.
summit.where: La Table du Grapiot, Pupillin; Le Bistronôme, Arbois; La Chaumière, Dole

lons.title: Lons eats regional
lons.story: Lons has no MICHELIN star or Bib; its own tables are regional bistros that Gault&Millau keeps in its selection. On rue Émile Monot, Ô Tablier seats 32 below street level and serves a short menu of morel crust in Vin Jaune, fondue and duck with Macvin. On rue de Vallière, Le Bistrot des Marronniers divides its menu between Lyon bouchon plates such as tablier de sapeur and Jura ones, grilling meat on a wood stove in the middle of the room. Out on the route de Besançon, La Petite Auberge (11/20) holds to Jura trout with bacon and a soufflé glacé flavoured with Macvin.
lons.where: Ô Tablier, Rue Émile Monot; Le Bistrot des Marronniers, Rue de Vallière; La Petite Auberge, Route de Besançon

wine.title: Arbois at table
wine.story: Jura wine is mostly drunk where it is made, and in Arbois it reaches the table with the food rather than over a tasting counter. On avenue Pasteur, La Finette has served Comté fondue and chicken in Vin Jaune at varnished log tables since 1961, from a list that holds only Jura bottles. Across town on Place Faramand, Le Bistrot des Claquets is a cave à manger: a bar from morning to about nine at night, one dish of the day at noon with a cold buffet, and the wine picked from a shelf of local natural growers. One is the old tavern, the other the growers' own canteen.
wine.where: La Finette, Arbois; Le Bistrot des Claquets, Arbois

street.title: Market squares, Morbier, chocolate
street.story: The Jura pantry is bought rather than eaten out, and most of it is cheese. In Lons the Thursday market, the largest in the department, runs from about seven to five across two squares, with the food stalls on Place de Verdun in the morning; a smaller organic market fills Cours Sully on Saturday mornings. Under the arcades at 39 rue du Commerce, Chez l'Artisan Fromager sells what the Poulet family make, as they have for four generations: raclette cheese, tomme du Jura and above all Morbier. In the centre at 1 rue Saint-Désiré, Pelen has made chocolate since 1899 and roasts its own beans.
street.where: Marché de Lons-le-Saunier, Place de Verdun; Chez l'Artisan Fromager, Rue du Commerce; Chocolaterie Pelen, Rue Saint-Désiré
